newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg has three bids for second GSM licence.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg has three bids for second GSM licence.

text.p: The Luxembourg Ministry of Communications said on Tuesday that three consortia had applied for a licence to operate the Grand Duchy's second GSM network.

The groups bidding to set up and run the GSM 900 Mhz network, which will challenge the only existing provider, P&T Luxembourg, are Letzgo S.A., LUXCALL S.A. and Millicom Luxembourg S.A., the ministry said in a statement.
No details of their offers were given.
The winner will be announced in late October.
Letzgo is made up of France Telecom Mobiles International, Banque Generale du Luxembourg SA (BGL) and its affiliate Cregelux, Belgium's Telinfo SA and Telindus SA and Luxembourg steel firm Arbed SA.

LUXCALL's shareholders are Cie Luxembourgeoise de Telecommunications SA (CL-COM), which is owned jointly by Cegedel and Audiolux - and Mannesman AG unit Mannesmann Eurokom GmbH, Cie Generale de Services et d'Applications de Telecommunications SA, a subsidiary of France's Cie Generale des Eaux.
Millicom Luxembourg is owned by Millicom International Cellular SA.
The ministry said all the consortia, as well as P&T Luxembourg had applied for an extension of the basic scope of the GSM licence on offer to cover spectra in the DCS 1800 frequency band as well.
P&T currently has about 50,000 customers, according to Luxembourg media.
P&T, which was obliged by law to respond to the tender process, was not immediately available for comment.
